Field notes: the tide gauge & the gull

The gauge on the north pile has been reading eleven centimetres high since the storm, and the fault is almost certainly mechanical rather than electronic: the float arm now fouls its guide near the top of the travel, which is exactly where the error appears.

Confirming that meant sitting on the pile for a full cycle with a staff gauge and a notebook, which is how I learned that a silver gull will investigate a notebook thoroughly if you put it down for even a moment.

The repair is a ten-minute job and a fortnight of paperwork. In the meantime the published series carries a correction flag, and anyone pulling it should honour that flag rather than the raw value.

Logged from the north pile, 0640 local
